## Install Julia {#sec-install-julia}

I recommend installing Julia using the `juliaup` tool, which will let you easily manage versions in the future and works seamlessly with VS Code. The instructions can be found at the [JuliaUp GitHub repository](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup), but we will summarize them here.

### Windows

You have two options:

1. **Windows Store (recommended)**: Install Juliaup [from the Windows Store](https://www.microsoft.com/store/apps/9NJNWW8PVKMN). This is the simplest method and handles `PATH` setup automatically.
2. **Command line**: Open **PowerShell** (search for it in the Start menu) and run:
   ```powershell
   winget install julia -s msstore
   ```
   Alternatively, if you have Git Bash installed, you can use the same `curl` command as macOS below.

### macOS

Open the **Terminal** app (found in Applications → Utilities) and run:

```shell
curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh
```

Follow the prompts; the installer will add Julia to your `PATH` automatically.

### Installing Julia 1.11.5

Once Juliaup is installed, open a terminal and run:

```shell
juliaup add 1.11.5
juliaup default 1.11.5
```

This installs Julia 1.11.5 and makes it the default version, which maximizes package compatibility throughout this course. Going forward, if you want to add new versions or change the default, you can [follow the Juliaup instructions](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup#using-juliaup).

### Verify your installation

Open a **new** terminal window (important — old windows won't see the updated `PATH`) and run:

```shell
julia --version
```

You should see something like `julia version 1.11.5`. You can also check your Juliaup configuration with:

```shell
juliaup status
```

This lists all installed Julia versions and shows which one is the default (marked with `*`).

## Opening the Julia REPL

The **REPL** (Read-Eval-Print-Loop) is Julia's interactive environment. To open it, open a terminal and type:

```shell
julia
```

You'll see a banner with the Julia version and a green `julia>` prompt where you can type Julia code. Type `exit()` or press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> to quit.

The REPL has several modes:

| Mode | How to enter | Prompt | Purpose |
|------|-------------|--------|---------|
| Julia | `julia` (default) | `julia>` | Run Julia code |
| Package | Type `]` | `pkg>` | Manage packages |
| Help | Type `?` | `help?>` | Access documentation |
| Shell | Type `;` | `shell>` | Run system commands |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**VS Code**: If you install the [Julia extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=julialang.language-julia) for VS Code, you can open a REPL directly inside the editor by pressing <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>J</kbd> then <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>O</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>J</kbd> then <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>O</kbd> (macOS).
:::

## Running a Julia Script

To run a `.jl` script from the terminal, use:

```shell
julia path/to/script.jl
```

For example, if you want to run a script named `hw.jl` in the current directory, you would type:

```shell
julia hw.jl
```

You can also run scripts from the REPL using `include`:

```julia
include("path/to/script.jl")
```

## Julia Environments and Packages

If your code returns an error when you try to load packages, it's possible you have a different version of Julia than the one the environment was set up for. In this case, delete the `Manifest.toml` file^[**Not** `Project.toml`!] and re-run a code block that contains:

```julia
import Pkg
Pkg.activate(@__DIR__)
Pkg.instantiate()
```

The line `Pkg.instantiate()` will install the right package versions for your installation and create a new `Manifest.toml` file.

## Troubleshooting

### `julia: command not found`

If your terminal says `command not found: julia` after installation:

- **Windows**: Restart your terminal. If you installed via the Windows Store and it still doesn't work, try reinstalling via the PowerShell `winget` method above, which handles `PATH` configuration more reliably. You can also add `%USERPROFILE%\.julia\juliaup\julia-1.11.5+0.x64\bin` to your system `PATH` manually through **System Properties → Environment Variables**.
- **macOS**: Juliaup adds itself to `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.zshrc`. Open a new terminal window to pick up the change. If that doesn't work, check that the following line exists in `~/.zshrc` (or `~/.bash_profile`):
  ```bash
  export PATH="$HOME/.juliaup/bin:$PATH"
  ```
  If it's missing, add it, then run `source ~/.zshrc` (or open a new terminal).

### The wrong Julia version runs

Run `juliaup status` to see your installed versions and which is marked as default (with `*`). If 1.11.5 is not the default:

```shell
juliaup default 1.11.5
```

If 1.11.5 isn't listed at all, install it first:

```shell
juliaup add 1.11.5
```

### Package installation errors

If you see errors like `unsatisfiable requirements` or package conflicts:

1. Delete the `Manifest.toml` file in the project folder.
2. Run `import Pkg; Pkg.activate(@__DIR__); Pkg.instantiate()` again (or restart the notebook/code block that does this).

If that doesn't work, make sure you're running Julia 1.11.5 (`julia --version`) and that the `Project.toml` file hasn't been modified.

### Julia REPL hangs or freezes

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> on macOS) to interrupt a running computation. To force-quit the REPL, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> or type `exit()`.
